description: Extend the iOS artefact chain from one core dylib to five, across native/ios/build-engine.sh, native/ios/project.yml, native/ios/package-ipa.sh and .github/workflows/ios.yml. A single divergence between what the build produces, what the project embeds, what the packaging fallback copies and what CI asserts is exactly what turns the macOS build red or ships an app that cannot find a core, so the same five canonical filenames must appear in all four files. Depends on FEAT-001.
steps: build-engine.sh: replace the single PS1 core step with a loop over the five cores. Take the filename list from `scripts/build-core.sh ios-names` rather than restating it, assert the list is exactly five entries so a broken list cannot silently verify nothing, call `scripts/build-core.sh ios-all` to build them, then check each expected dylib in build/lib/ and hard-fail naming every one that is missing. Keep the existing engine, UniFFI bindgen and switch-wrapper steps and the `--profile ios` plus target/aarch64-apple-ios/ios/ artefact paths exactly as they are.

build-engine.sh: keep the reasoning comment about why a missing core is a hard failure (an .ipa that launches and then cannot load its core is far harder to diagnose than a red build) and generalise it past PS1. Print each staged dylib with its size, as the PS1 step already did.

project.yml: add the four new dylibs to targets.Continuum.dependencies in the same shape as pcsx_rearmed (framework: build/lib/<name>, embed: true, link: false, codeSign: false), so all five land in Frameworks/ next to libcontinuum_switch.dylib. Comment once, above the group, that they are dlopened at runtime rather than linked and that package-ipa.sh signs everything in one later pass.

project.yml: leave the info.properties block completely intact (XcodeGen OVERWRITES Info.plist from it, so dropping a key drops it from the built app) and leave targets.Continuum.sources as ContinuumApp.swift, MetalCanvas.swift and build/Generated, because no new Swift file is added.

package-ipa.sh: replace the single PS1 fallback copy with a loop over the five canonical filenames, each reported by name when it has to be placed because Xcode's embed phase did not. Keep the ad-hoc signing loop over Frameworks/*.dylib and the `codesign --force --sign - --entitlements ... --generate-entitlement-der` pass on the bundle byte for byte, because that is what embeds the JIT and increased-memory entitlements TrollStore preserves.
package-ipa.sh: a missing dylib in build/lib must fail loudly there rather than producing an .ipa with a hole in it, since build-engine.sh already guaranteed the file exists.

ios.yml: in the Verify the .ipa step, keep the executable, Info.plist and libcontinuum_switch.dylib greps and add one grep per core dylib, each with its own ::error:: message naming the system that would not run, so a green tick still guarantees a useful build. Change nothing else in the workflow.
acceptance_criteria: build-engine.sh builds all five iOS cores and hard-fails, naming the file, if any expected dylib is absent from build/lib/.
build-engine.sh does not restate the five filenames: it reads them from `build-core.sh ios-names` and asserts there are five.
The engine, UniFFI and switch-wrapper steps, the `--profile ios` build and the target/aarch64-apple-ios/ios/ paths in build-engine.sh are unchanged.

project.yml lists all five dylibs with embed: true, link: false, codeSign: false, keeps its sources list correct and keeps info.properties intact including UIFileSharingEnabled and LSSupportsOpeningDocumentsInPlace.
package-ipa.sh's fallback covers all five dylibs and the ad-hoc entitlement signing behaviour is unchanged.
ios.yml greps for each of the five dylibs with its own ::error:: message and is otherwise unrestructured.
The same five canonical filenames appear in build-core.sh, project.yml, package-ipa.sh, ios.yml and ContinuumApp.swift, byte for byte.
verification: bash -n native/ios/build-engine.sh and bash -n native/ios/package-ipa.sh -> exit 0.

python3 yaml.safe_load on native/ios/project.yml and .github/workflows/ios.yml -> valid; assert all five dylibs appear in the target's dependencies and that info.properties still holds UIFileSharingEnabled and LSSupportsOpeningDocumentsInPlace.
A scripted cross-file grep of the five canonical filenames over the six files that must agree, reported as a trace.
The macOS build, xcodegen, xcodebuild and the .ipa contents cannot be produced here and are verified only by the orchestrator's CI run.
findings: build-engine.sh section 4 now reads the filename list from `build-core.sh ios-names`, asserts it has exactly five entries, CHECKS that all five names appear in project.yml, ios.yml and ContinuumApp.swift before compiling anything (those three restate the names by hand and no compiler can check them, so a typo would otherwise cost twenty minutes of core builds and then ship an app that cannot find a core), runs `ios-all`, and finally reports every staged dylib with its size while accumulating and hard-failing on any that is missing. The engine, UniFFI bindgen and switch-wrapper steps and the --profile ios / target/aarch64-apple-ios/ios/ paths are untouched. package-ipa.sh gained ROOT and loops the same ios-names list for its embed fallback, hard-failing if a core was never staged; the ad-hoc `codesign --force --sign - --timestamp=none` loop over Frameworks/*.dylib and the single `--entitlements ... --generate-entitlement-der` sign of the bundle are byte-identical, so the JIT and increased-memory entitlements TrollStore preserves are unaffected and the four new dylibs are sealed by the existing glob. project.yml embeds all five with embed:true link:false codeSign:false; sources and the 14-key info.properties block are unchanged. ios.yml's verify step greps each of the five with its own ::error:: naming the system that would not run; two further changes came from the review, both single-purpose rather than restructuring: timeout-minutes went 60 -> 120 because the build now compiles five native cores including an LTO CMake build and a full-depth submodule clone, and a timeout is this job's worst failure (no artefact, no annotation), and the XcodeGen step gained a conditional `command -v cmake || brew install cmake` because mgba's core build needs CMake on the host. VERIFIED: bash -n on both scripts; the cross-file check simulated end to end in this sandbox (count=5, all five present in all three consumers); yaml.safe_load on project.yml and ios.yml with assertions on the five dependencies, their embed flags, UIFileSharingEnabled and LSSupportsOpeningDocumentsInPlace; plistlib.load on Info.plist (20 keys); the five names traced across all six files.
